To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

autologous peripheral progenitor cell transplantation is feasible in an adult population of patients with acute myleogenous leukemia in first complete remission with no clear evidence of a benefit in leukemia-free or overall survival.
autologous transplant of IL-2- mobilized peripheral blood progenitors cells in adults with AML is feasible but does not improve leukemia-free survival.

autologous IL-2-mo-bilized peripheral blood progenitors cells are feasible in an un-selected population of adult patients, with minimal toxicity but with no clear evidence of improvement of leukemia-free survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient method for the treatment of leukemia in the elderly population, with the goal of improving the survival rate of these patients.
the development of a new method of in vivo tumor purging for autologous transplantation using IL-2 to mobilize progenitor cells.
the use of IL-2 to mobilize peripheral blood progenitor stem cells in order to improve the outcome for adult patients with leukemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of autologous IL-2-mobolized progenitor cells is not yet ready for routine clinical use in the treatment of patients with AML.
IL-2-mobolized peripheral blood progenitors are feasible to use but do not improve the outcome of AML in remission.
IL-2 mobilized autologous transplantation is not superior to standard mobilization with chemotherapy in patients with acute mylogenous leukemia in first remision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this trial are similar to those obtained in other centers with the use of autologous stem cell transplantation for AML in first remission.

the use of IL-2 as an in vivo purging strategy for autologous peripheral progenitor cell transplantation in patients with AML in first complete remission is feasible, safe and does not improve the results obtained in an age-matched control group of patients treated with autologously transplanted chemotherapy-mobilized peripheral progenitor cells.
autologous stem cell transplantation in AML in first CR is a feasible and safe procedure with a high rate of relapse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
autologous transplant of IL-2-primed progenitor cells in patients with AML in first remission is feasible, safe, and associated with rapid engraftment.

the use of IL-2 to mobilize progenitor cells in patients with acute myleogenous leukemia in first complete remission is feasible, but does not appear to improve outcomes compared with chemotherapy mobilization.
